items.text: Update 1.4 for Way of the Hunter 2 is now available on Steam. The Common Impala takes center stage in this update, giving you another species to encounter while exploring the landscapes of Kilimaya Reserve. But that’s not all! We’ve also been working on some important fixes based on your feedback, including improvements to shotguns and a fix for the missing taxidermy issues that have affected some of you.

We know how frustrating it has been to see your hard-earned trophies disappear from your hunting stands. Finding the cause of this issue and reproducing it reliably proved much more difficult than we initially expected, which meant it took us longer than we had hoped to find a solution. We’re sorry for the wait and the frustration this has caused.

With version 1.4, the issue should be fixed, and you should be able to place your missing trophies back on your hunting stands without running into the same problem again. Once you’ve updated the game, please tell us whether everything works as it should. Your feedback will help us make sure this is finally behind us.

As compensation for the taxidermy issue, all affected players will automatically receive 1,500 in-game currency for each taxidermy that disappeared from their dioramas. The fix restores the affected taxidermies present in the Hunting Log, yet missing from the lodge. While the taxidermies will not automatically reappear in your dioramas, you can now place them on your hunting stands again. The compensation covers the cost of the lost diorama placements.

Note for PC players with AMD GPUs: Some players with AMD graphics cards may experience crashes in Update 1.4. This is caused by a bug in the newest AMD drivers. In the meantime, we recommend rolling back to a previous driver version. We’re working on a hotfix.
For more details about version 1.4, please check the patch notes below.

Hunters, we’ve got another update ready for you! Alongside a bunch of fixes and improvements, this one brings a couple of highly requested features to Way of the Hunter 2. And one of them is a big one we’ve been looking forward to sharing with you for a long time.

notes.title: Non-Typical Mule Deer Trophies Are Here!

items.text: You asked for them, and now they’re finally here! Non-typical trophies have made their way into Way of the Hunter 2, bringing a new layer of variety and excitement to your hunting adventures.

Unlike typical trophies, non-typical animals can grow unusual antlers with extra points, irregular shapes, or other distinctive features. These rare finds stand out from the crowd, making every encounter a little more unpredictable and every successful hunt potentially even more memorable. You never know when an extraordinary animal might cross your path!

For now, non-typical trophies have been introduced for the Mule Deer. But this is just the beginning. As development continues, we plan to introduce non-typical trophies for more animal species, giving you even more unique animals to discover and harvest.
So keep your eyes open out there. You never know what might be hiding in the wilderness!
Another highly requested feature is finally here: HUD customization options!
You can now find these options in the game settings, where you can toggle individual HUD elements on or off to tailor your experience to your liking.

Want to switch off as much of the interface as possible and fully immerse yourself in the wilderness? Go for it. Prefer to keep useful information close at hand while tracking your next trophy? You can do that, too.
Whether you prefer a more immersive hunting experience or having all the essential information readily available, the choice is yours.
As always, we’ve also been working through the bugs and issues reported by the community, with a particular focus on UI-related problems.

One of the most important fixes addresses the issue of taxidermies disappearing from dioramas. We know how much time and effort you put into collecting your trophies and displaying them in your lodges, so we understand how frustrating this issue has been.
For those of you who have already been affected, we’re working to recover your missing taxidermies as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience while we work on this.
Your feedback continues to help us identify the issues that matter most, so please keep sharing your reports with us!
We’re keeping up the pace with updates even after release, and there’s plenty more on the horizon.

Alongside future free updates, we’re continuing work on exclusive gear DLCs and our upcoming new map, which is steadily moving closer to completion. There’s more hunting ahead, more equipment to discover, and more wilderness waiting to be explored.

items.text: Access the Shop from the laptop in your lodge or from the vicinity menu. Buy the ammo you want to bring with you. Note that:
You can carry 2 sets of ammo if you have no backpack, 4 with the default backpack, and 6 with the big backpack.
Each weapon has one ammo type that is default and free. Alternate ammo types are paid.

Access the storage and select the rifles/shotguns you want to bring with you. (Bows and arrows do not yet have alternate ammo - these will be added after full release).
Add your ammo to your ammo slots. You can fill multiple slots with the same ammo type.
Equip the ammo to your rifles.

items.text: Multiplayer arrives on the Default Branch, alongside a new rifle, a new suppressor, and a fresh round of fixes and improvements.
After the weekend of testing and improvements on the Experimental Branch, Update 0.4.1 is now live on the Default Branch of Way of the Hunter 2.

This update marks an important step for Way of the Hunter 2 as we bring Multiplayer to all players for the first time. It also introduces two new pieces of hunting gear — the CVA Cascade LRX bolt-action rifle and the Bergara Mercury Ti30 suppressor — alongside a wide range of fixes, tweaks, and improvements.
The wait is over. Multiplayer is now available on the Default Branch.
Two players can team up and head into the wilderness together, sharing the hunting experience and exploring the game side by side.

We've spent the past few weeks testing Multiplayer on the Experimental Branch, fixing issues and improving its stability based on your feedback. With this foundation now on the Default Branch, we'll continue working on expanding Multiplayer with more features and options in future updates.
We're excited to finally have you hunting together — and we're looking forward to seeing what you do with it.
Update 0.4.1 also adds the CVA Cascade LRX (.270 Winchester).
With its black finish and copper webbing matching the barreled action, the LRX stands out with a refined look while offering a capable platform for medium- and long-range shots.
Whether you're heading out for a carefully planned hunt or simply looking for a new rifle to add to your collection, the CVA Cascade LRX is ready to join your arsenal.

The Mercury Ti30 offers a refined balance of substantial sound reduction and premium handling. Its SLM-engineered baffle geometry is designed to maximize efficiency and reduce muzzle signature without compromising accuracy.
The Bergara Mercury Ti30 is being released as a real-world suppressor at the same time it arrives in Way of the Hunter 2, making this a unique day-one release both in-game and in the real world.
It's another option for hunters looking to keep their shots quieter while maintaining the precision needed for a successful hunt.
Alongside the new content and Multiplayer, Update 0.4.1 brings a broad range of fixes, tweaks, and improvements across the game.

The level progression and XP system has also been rebalanced. Following the rebalance, players may find that their updated level doesn't immediately appear after logging in. Gaining at least 1 additional XP point should trigger the correct level display. This is a temporary issue that we plan to resolve in a future update.
Heads-up: Please don't bring save files from Experimental back to the default branch, it could cause issues.

Over the past couple of weeks, we’ve been focusing heavily on fixing existing issues, polishing systems, and tweaking the gameplay based on your feedback. And once again, you’ve been incredibly helpful. Your reports, suggestions, and feedback have helped us move the game to a much better place as we approach the 1.0 launch.
Let’s take a look at what Update 0.4.0 brings to the game.

notes.title: Check out the new trailer here

items.text: A Brand-New Map

Update 0.4.0 introduces a completely new location for you to explore. This map is smaller than our full-sized hunting reserves, at roughly 16 km² / 6 square mi, but don't let its size fool you. It’s a new environment, inspired by the North American wildlife, already familiar from the game - the Wild Duck, Rocky Mountain Elk, Mule Deer, Snowshoe Hare, and Ptarmigan. New hunting opportunities, and places to discover also awaits here. Whether you want to explore every corner or simply enjoy a different hunting experience, there’s plenty waiting for you.
And this new location is also home to something much bigger…
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45898873/bc5f20296d243b45c078521e862e5345ef4bf5dd.png"]

Your new headquarters is a huge, fully upgradable lodge where you can bring together the trophies and accolades you’ve collected throughout your hunting adventures. As you progress, you’ll be able to gradually upgrade the lodge and shape it into a place that reflects your journey. Display your greatest trophies, showcase your achievements, and build a headquarters worthy of everything you’ve accomplished across the world of Way of the Hunter 2.
It’s your space, your collection, and your hunting legacy.

You'll also meet Elijah, a new NPC who's settled into the Headquarters. He'll walk you through what the place has to offer, from lodge upgrades to trophy displays to the shooting range, and he's always happy to talk about the other reserves and the animals waiting there too, so keep an ear out if you're curious about what's beyond the Headquarters.

A shooting range is also part of the Headquarters, we'll be expanding what you can do there in future updates, including trying out weapons you don't yet own. It's your space, your collection, and your hunting legacy.
We haven’t forgotten about the small game hunters! Update 0.4.0 adds two brand-new shotguns to your arsenal, including a very welcome addition from our friends at Merkel.
But new shotguns aren’t the only thing coming to the game. We’re also introducing shotgun choke.

Choke allows you to adjust how tightly the pellets from a shotgun shell are grouped as they leave the barrel. A tighter choke keeps the pellets concentrated over a longer distance, making it more suitable for longer shots, while a more open choke spreads the pellets out more quickly, which can be useful at shorter ranges. Alongside this, we've added a new pellet spread display to the Claim screen for shotgun kills, and a new dedicated organ for birds, air sacs, since these are such a defining part of the anatomy.
Based directly on your feedback, we've made several changes to how animals look, sound, and behave:
Crocodiles have been resized to better match their real-world scale, one of the most requested fixes from the community.
Duck AI has been improved, including flying and landing behavior, along with calling and decoying mechanics.
Vitals and skin materials have been updated for carnivores and several other species.
The sound of charging animals (Hippopotamus, Cape Buffalo, Southern Lion) has been improved, another change shaped by your feedback.
We've also rebalanced lethal damage, so high-energy calibers can now more reliably bring down animals.

Herd group sizes now grow or shrink over time based on how healthy the population is, healthier populations will support larger groups, while struggling ones will shrink. This ties directly into herd management and should make your work managing a reserve feel more meaningful over time.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45898873/76c5bcc70372675f97732e423eb5e93a08c07ebf.png"]

notes.title: More Control Over Your Hunting Experience

items.text: Update 0.4.0 also includes a number of highly requested quality-of-life improvements. One of them is the addition of separate audio sliders for animals and your dog. You can now fine-tune their volume independently and create the audio mix that works best for you.

We’re also expanding our in-game voice-over support to additional languages, meaning more players can now experience the game with voice acting they can understand. We've added localized voice overs in Chinese, French, German, Portuguese (Brasil) and Spanish (Latin-American).

We also went after some of the most persistent, annoying bugs many of you have run into: issues using gear while prone, timed jumps (bunny-hopping) no longer granting unintended extra speed, several taxidermy display issues, and a long list of UI improvements.

And, as always, this is just scratching the surface. This update contains over a hundred fixes, adjustments, and gameplay tweaks across the game. You can find the full details in the patch notes below.

Multiplayer on the Experimental Branch has received another substantial update as well. We fixed multiple synchronization issues affecting both host and client, animals, and vehicles, resolved several issues related to user markers, including their color coding and management, fixed trophies not being visible to clients, and made a number of other important improvements for stability and a more immersive multiplayer experience.

The result is a more solid multiplayer experience, and we're becoming increasingly confident that it will be ready to move to the default branch very soon, while we continue to work on it. In the meantime, if you want to jump in and test multiplayer with your friends, head over to the Experimental Branch and give it a try. Your feedback there is especially valuable as we continue preparing multiplayer for a wider release.

With the optimal caliber, animals now go down more reliably, without destroying excessive amounts of usable meat. Way of the Hunter 2 receives its first major content update, expanding the simulation with new systems and equipment that deepen both realism and player agency.

Players can now actively shape ecosystems through infrastructure improvements in reserves by restoring damaged habitats, removing pollution, and clearing invasive species. These efforts directly impact animal fitness and population potential, creating more dynamic and sustainable hunting grounds over time.

A new layer of tactical hunting is introduced with suppressors, allowing for quieter shots that reduce animal alertness and prevent nearby herds from spooking. This enables more controlled harvests and improved follow-up opportunities, encouraging careful, selective hunting strategies. The update also adds thermal optics, including both a handheld monocular and clip-ons. These tools allow players to detect heat signatures in low visibility conditions, offering multiple viewing modes for scanning terrain, tracking movement, and identifying targets with greater precision. Finally, Photo Mode is expanded with new player and dog poses, giving players more ways to capture both themselves and their hunting companions. These additions enhance storytelling and allow for more personalised and memorable in-game photography.

Animal behaviour has been refined, including fixes for frozen animals clustering across the map, alongside accurate trophy star ratings, improved tracking, and more realistic reactions. items.text: Hello hunters, a new patch for build 0.0.1 (187063) is now live. This patch includes several fixes, stability improvements, performance tweaks, and more.
Fixed: Issues with resolution and video settings not loading correctly
Fixed: Using binoculars could slowly reduce performance
Fixed: Voice-over autoplay after fast travel
Fixed: Dog-related crash when tracking animals that crossed water
Fixed: Crash after quitting to the main menu right after shooting
Fixed: Too many animal and footstep sounds playing at the same time could cause audio or performance issues
Fixed: Main menu music looping incorrectly
Tweaked: Reduced the character's fall damage

Known high-priority issue: Animals spawning in large groups outside their need zones and broken AI across the map. We are actively investigating this issue. Thank you for your patience while we work on a fix.

We are continuing to work on additional fixes and improvements based on your reports and feedback. If you run into bugs, please report them via THQN Redmine - ideally with your saved files attached - details on how to report a bug and attach your saved files can be found - HERE.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45898873/d2e86e0cbf14116776d1f1511b61d4c1dca38d43.png"]
We are also starting Community Feedback Rounds to collect more focused feedback and involve you more directly in shaping specific parts of the game during Early Access.

We have our own vision and direction for the game, but we also want to hear your observations, ideas, and constructive feedback - both from your in-game experience and your real-life hunting experience. We’ll be running these feedback rounds regularly, most likely in two-week cycles, each focused on specific features, animals, systems, or gameplay elements.
The first feedback round runs from April 1 to April 14. During this time, we will collect your feedback on:
Mule deer antlers & trophy
Turkeys
Please keep the feedback constructive, specific, and based on your experience - both in-game and in real life.
Thank you for being part of the Early Access journey with us. We really appreciate the time you spend playing and sharing your thoughts.
Happy hunting!

A new patch for build 0.0.1 (Version: 188484) is now live. This patch addresses several reported gameplay issues and includes a fix for the frozen animal groups that affected a lot of players. The fix should prevent it from happening again. If you still have frozen animal groups on your map, please cull them - they should not reappear afterwards. As this issue was difficult to reproduce consistently, we are marking it as a potential fix. If this issue occurs again or if you stumble upon some new bugs, please report them via THQN Redmine - details on how to report a bug and attach your saved files can be found HERE.
We are continuing to monitor your feedback and work on further improvements.
Fixed: Duplicated NPCs spawning near the cabins
Fixed: Animals now correctly react to gunshot sounds when fired from behind cover (e.g. bushes)
Fixed: Discard button for displayed trophies
Potential fix: Animals getting stuck (freezing in place in large groups)
Players affected by this issue may still have large groups of frozen animals present on their map. In this case, please cull all affected animals - the issue should not occur again afterwards.
Please note this is a potential fix, since we were not able to reproduce the issue consistently during testing.
If the issue occurs again, please report it via THQN Redmine, including any additional details (what actions were taken, steps before it happened, etc.) - thank you!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45898873/c6ce8b0584d3041d98296afffa10264c241840d7.png"]
Community feedback round #1 is now closed

At the same time, we are closing the first community feedback round. Thank you to everyone who participated and shared their thoughts, observations, and real-life experiences on the Turkeys and Mule deer trophies - your input is incredibly valuable and helps us shape the game during Early Access.
More feedback rounds are on the way, so stay tuned!
Thank you for your continued support and for being part of the Early Access journey with us.
Happy hunting!
